description:
Found by the fz-da session while spiking fz-3sy.21 (its struct!/2 helper); reduced here. Verified on develop ac3750d1e + #454, interp path. OptionParser's fz-sc8.127 spike (targets are the call authority) does not fix it.

Repro (scratch cf/n1.fz in the fz-xxd13-build session):

defmodule S do
  def a(fields), do: build(%{x: 0}, fields, false)
  def b(fields), do: build(%{x: 0}, fields, true)

  defp build(base, fields, flag) do
    Enum.reduce(fields, base, fn key, acc -> missing(key, acc, flag) end)
  end

  defp missing(_key, acc, false), do: acc
  defp missing(key, acc, true), do: Map.put(acc, key, 0)
end

def main() do
  IO.inspect(S.a([:x]))
  IO.inspect(S.b([:y]))
end

Elixir prints %{x: 0} then %{x: 0, y: 0}. fz2 interp fails at run time: "backend dispatch callsite in executable ExecutableKey { ... } missed an exhaustive dispatch". fz-da reports the run path exits 132 on its fuller program.

What the variants show:
- Passes when both callers pass the same element type (S.a([:y]) and S.b([:y])).
- Passes with one caller only (either one).
- Fails with a list accumulator instead of a map (n2.fz), and with Map.put(acc, :x, 0) (n4.fz), so the map is not the cause.
- An integer version (elements [1, 2] at both callers, pick/3 with false/true clauses) passes.
So the ingredients are: one closure construction, a captured flag that is false at one caller and true at the other, and element types that differ between the callers (:x vs :y).

Mechanism not established. The dispatch on the captured flag inside missing/3 (or the closure's own dispatch) is built as exhaustive for fewer (flag, element) pairings than run time delivers.

Done when: the repro prints Elixir's output on interp, run and build, as a fixture (fz-sc8 block, 01140 onward).

comments.text: Unchanged by fz-sc8.127 (7764bbe51, OptionParser's check): interp reports the missed exhaustive dispatch and run exits 132 on base and change binaries.

title: Two callers of a helper whose reducer captures a flag run without a missed dispatch
